text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers:
- The government on Thursday rejected petrol traders' calls for a 9.5 to 11 percent rise in petrol prices.
- According to unofficial sources there is a good chance the conservative People's Party may form a coalition with the centre-left Liberal Democrats of Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek.
- On Friday repairs will begin on part of highway beetwen Ljubljana and Postojna, Slovenia's Motorway Company said. Traffic will be partly restricted until October 30.

- Miran Mejak, head of Slovenia's negotiating group in the process of dividing assets of the former Yugoslavia, said on Thursday a meeting with international coordinator Sir Arthur Watts had yielded no results.
- Slovenia's under-21 ski-jumping team won a golden medal at the under-21 world championship in Calgary.
- The Croatian government on Thursday agreed to start negotiations on a free trade deal with Slovenia.
- The parliament has not yet decided upon the procedure to be adopted for returning large forest estates that were nationalised after World War Two to their owners.

- Analysts said foreign portfolio investors may be forced to take tolar loans in Slovenia in order to buy Slovenian securities following recent decrees by the Bank of Slovenia regarding foreign portfolio investment.
